subject: EVS
central_question: How can observing changes over a day and a year help us recognise the repeating natural rhythms that shape plants, animals and human life?
in_scope_units: Changes over time: Saba and Aparna compare changes in themselves, school and surroundings.
Changes at different speeds: years, yearly repetition, days, minutes and seconds.
Changes Around Us in a Day—Day and Night: the apparent movement of the Sun and the cause of day and night.
Activity 1 and Day–Night Demonstration: a student model, torch and rotating globe.
Globe: a model of Earth, land masses, seas and oceans.
Changes Around Us in a Year—Seasons’ Journal: observing the same surroundings over time.
Classroom Seasons’ Chart, Steps 1–4: time periods, five themes, posters and seasonal stories.
Discovering Seasons: repeating yearly patterns and six named seasons.
Regional differences: winter and monsoon differ across India.
Celebrating Seasons: songs, crops and festivals linked with seasons.
Let us reflect, Questions 1–6: experiences, local names, food, clothes, festivals, nature, journaling and drawings.
banned_topics: Worldwide trade and movement of foods, birds and ideas from Chapter 10.
Electricity and clean-energy experiments from Chapter 7.

known_pitfalls.claim: Day and night happen because the Sun circles Earth every day.
known_pitfalls.correction: The torch-and-globe demonstration shows Earth rotating while the Sun is represented by a steady torch.

known_pitfalls.claim: A season is any one-time change in weather.
known_pitfalls.correction: A season is a natural pattern that repeats every year.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every part of India experiences a season in exactly the same way.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter compares Kerala with Kashmir and Assam with Rajasthan to show regional differences.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Seasons’ Chart records only weather.
known_pitfalls.correction: It also records plants, animals, water and human activities.

recommended_example_progression: Opening NCERT Write table: classify changes in self, school and surroundings.
NCERT Activity 1: explain day and night through Earth’s rotation.
NCERT Classroom Seasons’ Chart, Steps 1–2: organise observations.
NCERT Steps 3–4: identify patterns by theme and by time period.
NCERT six-season table: connect local months with six season names.
NCERT Let us reflect, Question 4: compare food, clothes, festivals and nature.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter section is ‘Let us reflect’, Questions 1–6 on pages 159–160.
